title: Using keyboard manager shortcut to activate systray minimised application does not restore window correctly
author: insanityinside
summary: Keyboard Manager's Run Program/activation shortcut exposes hidden KeePass/KeePassXC windows instead of asking the existing application to restore its intended tray window.

confidence.rationale: The symptom strongly matches broad window restoration, but the exact current activation implementation and app-specific single-instance behavior need reproduction.

judgment.rationale: The report identifies two affected applications and a specific tray-minimized state. The likely window-selection behavior can be reproduced locally without asking the reporter for maintainer-side investigation.
evidence: Activating tray-minimized KeePassXC through a Keyboard Manager shortcut restores a hidden Qt window and prevents normal restore.
KeePass similarly exposes multiple normally hidden windows.
The issue explicitly observes that all windows from the process appear to be made visible.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the existing-instance activation path and restrict restoration to an appropriate top-level application window or native activation contract.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The cross-app evidence supports a focused plan: prefer application-native single-instance activation, otherwise rank/filter eligible top-level windows and never reveal hidden helper windows indiscriminately.

proposed_fixes.title: Avoid restoring hidden helper windows for Run Program actions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The existing-process activation path likely shows multiple top-level windows owned by the executable instead of selecting the application's intended restorable window or relying on its single-instance activation.
plan: Trace Run Program handling when an executable already exists and inventory which windows are enumerated/restored.
Filter out owned/tool/hidden helper windows and prefer an eligible visible/minimized main window; if no safe target exists, launch normally and let the app's single-instance contract activate itself.
Add tests around window eligibility/ranking and app-compat verification with KeePassXC and KeePass tray modes.
verification: Minimize KeePassXC to tray, invoke the shortcut, and confirm only the intended main window restores.
Repeat with KeePass and with a normal minimized single-window application; verify no hidden helper windows become visible.

confidence.rationale: The symptom strongly matches broad window restoration, but the exact current activation implementation and app-specific single-instance behavior need reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager's Run Program/activation shortcut exposes hidden KeePass/KeePassXC windows instead of asking the existing application to restore its intended tray window.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.79.0 and KeePassXC 2.7.6.
The application is configured to hide to the system tray when minimized.
The issue is labeled Area-App Compat and Needs-Repro.
inferences: Keyboard Manager may enumerate process windows and call a show/restore operation without filtering tool, owner, hidden helper, or application-main windows.
issue_context.analysis: The cross-app evidence supports a focused plan: prefer application-native single-instance activation, otherwise rank/filter eligible top-level windows and never reveal hidden helper windows indiscriminately.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue, both comments, labels, and named application behavior.
Used KeePass and KeePassXC exhibiting the same hidden-window symptom as evidence of a generic activation path.

reproduce.title: Activate KeePassXC from a Keyboard Manager Run Program shortcut
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: KeePassXC with tray icon and hide-on-minimize enabled
setup: Create a Keyboard Manager shortcut that runs KeePassXC.
Launch KeePassXC and minimize it to the system tray.
steps: Record every window made visible and whether the main window can still be restored.
Optionally repeat with KeePass to compare helper-window behavior.
reproduce.expected_result: When an instance already exists in the tray, only its intended main window should restore; hidden helper windows must remain hidden.
